title: The Quran: Surah 57, al-Hadid (The Iron), verse 20
author: Tradução inglesa de Talal Itani (ClearQuran)
tradition: Texto sagrado do Islão, século VII
intro: Lição sobre a Surata 57, versículo 20. O texto inglês é a tradução de Talal Itani, reproduzida sem alterações; as notas de língua, perguntas, discussão e escrita são material pedagógico separado, baseado apenas no que o próprio texto diz.

source.title: Quran English Translation: Clear, Pure, Easy to Read Modern English
source.edition: Edition A (uses the word 'Allah' to refer to the Creator)

questions.q: According to the verse, what is the worldly life compared to?
questions.why: O versículo diz: 'It is like a rainfall that produces plants'.

questions.q: The verse says the plants grow, wither, turn yellow and become debris. What does this list show?
options: A process of change over time
questions.why: Cada passo segue o anterior: produz, murcha, amarelece, fica em restos.

questions.q: Which list does the first sentence contain?
options: Play, distraction, glitter, boasting and rivalry
questions.why: A primeira frase lista 'play, and distraction, and glitter, and boasting... and rivalry'.

questions.q: Which sentence best sums up the verse?
options: The worldly life is compared to rain that gives plants that then dry up, while the Hereafter is described differently
The worldly life is a long journey
The worldly life is a battle
The worldly life is a feast
questions.why: O versículo compara a vida terrena a chuva e plantas e depois contrasta com o Além.

B2.discussion: The verse compares life to plants that grow and then dry up. Which other picture from nature could describe how things change?
B2.writing: Write 80 to 100 words: Describe in your own words the picture of the plants in this verse.

questions.q: What does the rainfall produce, and who does it delight, according to the verse?
options: Plants, and it delights the disbelievers
Rivers, and it delights the poor
Gold, and it delights the traders
Fire, and it delights the strong
questions.why: O versículo diz 'a rainfall that produces plants, and delights the disbelievers'.

options: competition between people about wealth and children

questions.q: 'Delights the disbelievers' comes before 'But then it withers'. What does this order create?
options: A contrast between a pleasant start and a poor end
questions.why: O 'But then' separa o agrado do murchar.

questions.q: How does the verse organise its argument?
options: A story, a dialogue, a list, a prayer, a rule
A list, a comparison, a change in stages, a contrast with the Hereafter, a closing statement
questions.why: O versículo tem cinco frases, cada uma com uma função.

options: The verse describes the worldly life through things that seem lively but pass away
The verse describes the worldly life as endless
The verse describes the worldly life as a battle
The verse does not describe the worldly life
questions.why: 'Play', 'glitter', plantas que murcham e 'enjoyment of vanity' apontam para coisas que passam.

C1.discussion: The verse builds its comparison in stages, from rain to debris. How does this step by step order affect the way the reader takes in the image?
C1.writing: Write 120 to 150 words: Explain how the picture of the rain and the plants supports the first sentence of the verse.

questions.q: What does the verse say is in the Hereafter?
options: Severe agony, forgiveness from Allah, and acceptance
questions.why: O versículo diz 'severe agony, and forgiveness from Allah, and acceptance'.

options: a repetition of the first sentence
a contrast with the life described before
questions.why: 'While' introduz o contraste com a vida terrena.

questions.q: The last sentence returns to the idea of the first. What does it do?
options: It ends with a list of names
It closes the verse by returning to its starting point in a shorter sentence
questions.why: A última frase diz 'The life of this world is nothing but enjoyment of vanity', e resume o que a primeira lista.

questions.q: Which pattern appears in the first sentence?
questions.why: A primeira frase junta cinco itens com 'and'.

questions.q: Which description of the verse is best supported?
options: A list, then an extended image of plants growing and withering, then a contrast, then a short closing line
questions.why: As cinco frases cumprem essas funções, uma a uma.

C2.discussion: The verse uses one extended image, rain and plants, to carry its whole argument. What does an extended image do that a list of qualities cannot?
C2.writing: Write 150 to 200 words: Analyse how the verse is built from its first sentence to its last, referring to specific words.
